research_question: Do fitted Jacobian lenses converge and merge consistently at 10 and 25 prompts?
result: ENGINEERING_IMPROVING: 7 of 9 criteria passed; shard-merge vs direct max_abs 2.38e-07 (limit 1e-05); the two 10-vs-25 convergence criteria failed (relative Frobenius 0.4170 vs limit 0.10; cosine 0.9205 vs limit 0.99)
limitations: Engineering convergence only; the 10-prompt set is nested inside the 25-prompt set so this measures estimator movement, not independent replication; one T4, one model revision, one corpus, one run per configuration with no repeated-measure variance; top-k overlap and rank correlation are technical stability evidence and never semantic evidence

research_question: Does parser v3 correct the parser-v2 failure modes without overfitting?
result: 9 development gates passed and 1 NOT_APPLICABLE; 60/60 non-regression and 65/65 adversarial typed agreement
limitations: Development gates only; parser v3 is NOT validated; the 65 adversarial fixtures share authorship with the parser so they are not an independent oracle; all five rule changes are recall-increasing so precision is unprobed; the two retired mismatch cases were not read and remain unaddressed

research_question: Is an independent parser-v3 locked holdout constructed and sealed with zero overlap?
result: 0 unresolved labels across 120 cases in 12 strata; 113/120 whole-row reviewer agreement pre-arbitration with 7 rows arbitrated; 0 exact and 0 normalized collisions against every reachable prior corpus
limitations: Construction only; the set is NOT sealed to immutable storage this round, so the holdout is not yet locked and no parser-v3 evaluation may be run against it; reviewer agreement is LLM operational consensus, not human ground truth; isolation between construction and parser-v3 development is procedural, not security-enforced, and both happened in the same worktree; the overlap check against the retired parser-v2 locked inputs was attempted and BLOCKED by a wedged Azure Run Command extension, so it is recorded as NOT PERFORMED
